title: Give every tenant's handler its own routes

blocks.text: The invoicing service runs one router for many tenants. Each tenant gets its own handler, `new InvoiceHandler("northwind")`, whose `paths()` builds `/northwind/invoices` and `/northwind/invoices/{id}` from the tenant it was given. The first version of the new `Handler` base class built each handler's routes as the handler was created, and every tenant's handler registered `/null/invoices`: every invoice request got a 404. The router asks each handler for its `routes()` when it registers it, and again on every configuration reload, a few times a minute.

Finish `routes()` in `src/main/java/practice/Handler.java`. When you're done, every handler serves the paths its own `paths()` builds from its own fields, and a reload hands back the same routes without making the handler build its paths again. Subclasses of `Handler` stay as they are. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a handler whose paths depend on nothing of its own serves exactly those paths
a handler whose paths use a field its own constructor sets serves paths built from that field's value, not from its default
asking a handler for its routes again returns the same routes without building its paths again

origin.section: Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default

concepts: A superclass constructor that calls an overridable method runs the subclass's override before the subclass's fields are assigned; build such state on first use instead.
